message.content:
**Hydrogen (H)** – the simplest and most abundant element in the universe – has a rich set of physical, chemical, and nuclear properties that make it unique among the elements. Below is a comprehensive overview grouped into key categories:

| Category | Property | Value / Description |
|----------|----------|---------------------|
| **Atomic & Nuclear** | Atomic number | 1 |
| | Atomic mass (average) | 1.008 u |
| | Isotopes | Protium (^1H, 99.98 %), Deuterium (^2H or D, 0.02 %), Tritium (^3H or T, radioactive, half‑life ≈ 12.32 yr) |
| | Nuclear spin | ^1H: ½, ^2H: 1, ^3H: ½ |
| | Magnetic moment | ^1H: 2.7928 μ_N, ^2H: 0.857 μ_N, ^3H: 2.978 μ_N |
| | Ionization energy | 13.598 eV (first ionization) |
| | Electron affinity | –0.754 eV (negative, meaning H⁻ is unstable in vacuum) |
| | Electronegativity (Pauling) | 2.20 |
| | Standard enthalpy of formation (ΔH_f°) | 0 kJ mol⁻¹ (by definition for elemental H₂) |
| | Standard Gibbs free energy of formation (ΔG_f°) | 0 kJ mol⁻¹ |
| | Standard entropy (S°) | 130.68 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ (for H₂ gas at 298 K) |
| **Physical (gas)** | State at STP | Colorless, odorless, tasteless, highly flammable gas |
| | Boiling point | –252.87 °C (121.5 K) |
| | Melting point | –259.16 °C (14.0 K) |
| | Density (at 0 °C, 1 atm) | 0.08988 g L⁻¹ (≈ 0.00008988 kg m⁻³) |
| | Molar volume (ideal gas) | 22.414 L mol⁻¹ (at 0 °C, 1 atm) |
| | Diffusivity | Extremely high; H₂ diffuses ~10× faster than N₂ in air |
| | Speed of sound in H₂ | ~1270 m s⁻¹ (at 20 °C) |
| | Specific heat ratio (γ) | 1.41 (diatomic ideal gas) |
| | Viscosity | 8.76 × 10⁻⁶ Pa·s (at 300 K) |
| | Refractive index | 1.000132 (at 589 nm, 20 °C) |
| | Ionization potential (photoionization) | 13.598 eV |
| | Spectral lines | Lyman series (UV), Balmer series (visible), Paschen series (IR) |
| **Chemical (reactivity)** | Bond type | Diatomic covalent (H–H) |
| | Bond dissociation energy | 436 kJ mol⁻¹ (≈ 4.52 eV) |
| | Oxidation states | +1 (most common), –1 (hydride), 0 (elemental) |
| | Acidic behavior | Forms hydronium (H₃O⁺) in aqueous solution; strong acid when protonated |
| | Basic behavior | Forms hydride (H⁻) in metal hydrides; weak base in organometallics |
| | Combustion reaction | 2 H₂ + O₂ → 2 H₂O (exothermic, ΔH ≈ –286 kJ mol⁻¹) |
| | Reaction with metals | Forms metal hydrides (e.g., NaH, CaH₂) |
| | Reaction with halogens | Forms hydrogen halides (HF, HCl, HBr, HI) |
| | Reaction with oxygen | Forms water vapor; can form ozone (O₃) under UV |
| | Reaction with nitrogen | Forms ammonia (NH₃) via Haber process (N₂ + 3 H₂ → 2 NH₃) |
| | Reaction with carbon monoxide | Forms formic acid (HCOOH) or methanol (CH₃OH) under catalytic conditions |
| | Redox behavior | Acts as reducing agent (e.g., in hydrogenation reactions) |
| | Solubility in water | 1.6 g L⁻¹ at 25 °C (≈ 0.018 mol L⁻¹) |
| | Solubility in organic solvents | Variable; generally soluble in nonpolar solvents (e.g., hexane) |
| | Electrochemical potential | Standard hydrogen electrode (SHE) defined as 0 V |
| **Isotopic & Nuclear** | Deuterium (²H) | Stable, used in heavy water (D₂O) as neutron moderator |
| | Tritium (³H) | Radioactive β⁻ emitter; used in fusion research and radiolabeling |
| | Fusion reaction | D + T → He‑4 + n + 17.6 MeV (key for fusion energy) |
| | Nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) | ^1H NMR widely used in chemistry and medicine (MRI) |
| | Magnetic resonance imaging | Proton (hydrogen) signals provide contrast in human tissues |
| **Spectroscopic** | Lyman series (UV) | Transitions from n=2,3,… to n=1 |
| | Balmer series (visible) | Transitions from n=3,4,… to n=2 (e.g., Hα at 656.3 nm) |
| | Paschen series (IR) | Transitions from n=4,5,… to n=3 |
| | Infrared absorption | H–H stretch at ~4160 cm⁻¹ (ν₁) |
| | Raman scattering | Strong H₂ Raman line at ~4155 cm⁻¹ |
| | Microwave transitions | Rotational transition at 1420 MHz (21 cm line) – key for radio astronomy |
| **Miscellaneous** | Flame color | Blue (blue‑white) due to electronic transitions |
| | Combustion temperature | ~2,800 °C (in stoichiometric mixture) |
| | Pressure in stars | Hydrogen fusion powers the Sun; core temperature ~15 million K |
| | Role in cosmology | First element formed in Big Bang nucleosynthesis; primordial abundance ~75 % by mass |

---

### Quick Reference Summary

- **Element**: Hydrogen (H)
- **Atomic number**: 1
- **Common isotopes**: Protium (^1H), Deuterium (^2H), Tritium (^3H)
- **State at STP**: Gas (colorless, odorless, flammable)
- **Boiling point**: –252.9 °C
- **Density**: 0.0899 g L⁻¹
- **Bond dissociation energy**: 436 kJ mol⁻¹
- **Oxidation states**: +1, 0, –1
- **Key reactions**: Combustion → H₂O, Haber process → NH₃, fusion → He⁴ + n
- **Spectral lines**: Lyman, Balmer, Paschen, 21 cm line
- **Applications**: Fuel (hydrogen economy), MRI, NMR spectroscopy, fusion research, heavy water moderator, radiolabeling

Feel free to ask for deeper details on any specific property or application!
